conclusions.rationale: Re-evaluated against the complete current context: accepted-start capture before Handy surfaces, successful-start commit, stable platform identity/PID/name/icon reference, explicit-choice-only mutation and queued/cancelled/PID-reuse tests satisfy the criterion. The stack frontmatter date/title change affects no architecture, capture semantics or test seam.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-001

**Criterion:** When a dictation starts and the frontmost application is not Handy, Handy records its identity (bundle identifier on macOS; application user model ID on Windows when available, otherwise executable path), display name, icon and process id. Application switches during the recording, processing and AI step do not change it. When Handy is frontmost, no destination is recorded.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 1

plan_citations.excerpt: Capture when a recording actually starts, including a queued coordinator press when it drains, not when a key press was remembered while busy.

macOS identity is bundle identifier; PID and process start identity defend against PID reuse. Windows prefers AUMID, otherwise canonical executable path; keep HWND only as an activation hint, not field-level authority.
New inline Rust tests cover immutable capture, explicit choices and cross removal/no-op/insertion-boundary races, queued actual-start capture, restart/PID reuse and stale/cancelled generations.

conclusions.rationale: The current plan retains one-shot resolve/activation with a worker-owned monotonic one-second deadline, late-callback cancellation and a fresh target check at actual dispatch after the preserved paste delay. None/off/no-target paths do not activate. Existing method bytes, clipboard policy and auto-submit remain unchanged while waits/process waiting move off the UI thread. Deadline, focus-loss and native heartbeat tests make the requirement verifiable; native feasibility remains an implementation gate.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-002

**Criterion:** With "Return to the dictation's application" on (default on where supported), before insertion Handy activates the destination and waits until it is frontmost, for at most 1 second and without freezing Handy's interface, re-checks that it is still frontmost immediately before inserting (a failed re-check counts as an activation failure, without retry), then runs the configured insertion method unchanged. With the paste method "none" no application is activated. With the setting off, or without a destination, insertion targets the frontmost application as today.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Stories 1 and 5

plan_citations.excerpt: The 1 s deadline bounds activation request scheduling and foreground observation only.
Brief AppKit/native requests run on main thread via returned channels; all deadline waiting happens on worker/Tokio.
Off/unsupported/no destination/FrontmostAtEnd retains current insertion policy and does not activate a captured app.
Its guard runs **after paste_delay_ms**, immediately before first emitted key/text or external-script launch, with no clipboard-policy side effects for an unavailable destination.

conclusions.rationale: Badge icon/name or Frontmost app, accessible label and hidden states for off/unsupported/overlay-none are explicitly implemented and tested in Step 5. Destination logic remains active without the badge surface. Deferred design generation is authorized in the source; planned flow/screen IDs and bound approval before UI code are retained without false visual certification.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-003

**Criterion:** While the indicator is visible and "Return to the dictation's application" is on and supported, a badge next to it shows the destination icon and name, or "Frontmost app" without a destination. The badge has the accessible name "Destination: <name>". When the setting is off or unsupported, no badge is shown. With the overlay style set to none, no badge is shown and the destination behavior still applies.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 2

plan_citations.excerpt: **AC covered:** AC-003: badge label and visibility; AC-004: one-click cross with accessible label, event isolation and insertion-entry freeze; foreground-first menu, current-session choices, dismiss unchanged, ≤200 ms update, insertion close and no keyboard focus capture; AC-007: unsupported reason.

**Success criteria:** Icons/names or Frontmost app, badge hidden for off/unsupported/none, cross clears only current destination without menu/focus/settings side effects; menu first/remaining/end ordering, dismiss unchanged and insertion closes/rejects choices; keyboard remains with app.

conclusions.rationale: The one-click cross uses the same FrontmostAtEnd session mutation as the menu, leaves the persistent boolean unchanged, stops propagation and carries a localized Remove destination label. Version/session/phase checks freeze selection at insertion and reject queued clicks. Menu foreground-first/windowed deduplication, Handy exclusion, current marking, unchanged dismissal, 200 ms update and non-key pointer surface all have concrete tests and native proof.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-004

**Criterion:** Until insertion begins, the badge shows a cross control: one click on it removes the destination of the current dictation (badge "Frontmost app", text inserted into the application frontmost at the end), as the menu entry "Frontmost app at the end" does; the cross has the accessible name "Remove destination". Clicking the badge itself opens a menu listing the application frontmost now first (Handy excluded), then other running applications that have windows, each with icon and name, and "Frontmost app at the end". Choosing an entry changes the destination of the current dictation only and updates the badge within 200 ms; dismissing keeps it. When insertion begins, an open menu closes and later choices are ignored. Opening and using the menu does not take keyboard focus from the user's application.
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 3

plan_citations.excerpt: The badge cross calls the same FrontmostAtEnd selection mutation as the menu entry: one click clears only this session, leaves the persistent setting unchanged, and updates the badge within 200 ms.
Give the cross its own localized accessible name "Remove destination"; stop event propagation so its click does not open the menu or take keyboard focus.
At menu-open read frontmost before touching surface focus, list that non-Handy app first, then deduplicated other running applications with user windows, and finally Frontmost app at the end.
Then the frozen selection is unchanged and the command is rejected

conclusions.rationale: All unavailable-target branches fail closed without fallback or retry. Actual WAV/save results govern history claims and a bounded opaque native reference preserves failure text. Visible reasons last four seconds from presentation even across a new recording; 010 later inherits that minimum via acknowledged ownership. Overlay-none without 010 is explicitly staged as missing bubble capability, never certified as recovered. Fault/consumer/history matrices and native reason timing cover the final intended behavior.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-005

**Criterion:** If the destination is no longer running, is not frontmost within 1 second of activation, or the insertion method reports failure, no text is sent to any other application; the transcript stays in history whenever history saving succeeds as today, the indicator displays the reason (app closed, activation failed, insertion failed) for at least 4 seconds (with the overlay style none, the recovery bubble of 010 carries the reason), and the transcript is handed to the recovery bubble (010).
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

plan_citations.excerpt: History guarantee is explicitly conditional as AC-005/SC-002 require: keep existing WAV-gated save, never claim history when WAV or save_entry fails.

While 010 is absent, visible-overlay failures use a dedicated reason state in the indicator for **at least 4 s measured from visible presentation**; do not run the unconditional hide-after-paste path first.
010 inherits the ≥4 s minimum reason visibility obligation from 006; its AC-001 replaces the surface, not conservation or truthful status.
**Success criteria:** No destination retry/fallback on chosen-app failure; guard before input, none/cancel no activation, old frontmost behavior for off/no destination/unsupported.

conclusions.rationale: Current AC-006 permits method-owned verified evidence. The plan preserves inserted, verified after 007 read-back as exact method_outcome while destination status remains insertion_attempted and destination makes no verification claim of its own. It waits for 007 terminal results, routes uncertain/not-read failures to 010 without Enter, preserves the three eligible method results for 009 guards, and leaves AX fallback and all clipboard timing/restoration with 007. The 008 framework is reused for configuration rather than copied.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-006

**Criterion:** Destination, insertion method and clipboard handling are separate settings and steps: this feature decides only which application is activated. Handy passes the insertion method's outcome (for smart paste, the outcomes of 007) to the recovery bubble (010) and to automatic Enter (009), reports "insertion attempted" when the method reports success, and never reports that text was verified in a field except when the method itself verified it (the smart paste outcome "inserted, verified" of 007, based on reading the field back).
**Priority:** P1 | **Story:** Story 4

plan_citations.excerpt: Map inserted, verified/read observed/typed to insertion_attempted in the destination status, preserving exact method_outcome and its method-owned evidence; 006 never produces a field verification claim.

Map not read/permission missing/uncertain/insertion failed to failed with insertion_failed reason while preserving the exact method detail; clipboard handed over to clipboard_handed_over, neither attempted field insertion nor failure.
These decisions and all timers are owned by 007, never reimplemented or reset by 006.
Then destination status is insertion_attempted with exact inserted, verified method_outcome

conclusions.rationale: The macOS/Windows workspace adapters and their separate native proof cover support; Linux or unreadable foreground reports an unavailable reason and retains current insertion behavior with hidden badge/disabled toggle and no forced persisted value. Readable Handy frontmost is a supported no-destination case. Failure after capturing a valid target remains a destination failure instead of reverting to legacy insertion.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-007

**Criterion:** Support is macOS and Windows. On Linux, and wherever the frontmost application cannot be read, the setting is shown as unavailable on this system with the reason, and insertion behaves as today.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

plan_citations.excerpt: Linux is explicitly unsupported; macOS/Windows become unsupported when frontmost cannot be read.
Unsupported state is `{available:false, reason}` with old insertion behavior, hidden badge and disabled toggle with localized explanation; no persisted forced false and no silent write.
A failure after a valid destination was captured is activation_failed/app_closed, never a switch to the legacy frontmost path.

conclusions.rationale: The destination boolean extends the existing 008 output descriptor/PublicSettings and exact shared read_snapshot/commit_mutation/SettingsMutation/LiveSettingsEffects service. UI and CLI share capability/type validation, latest-state locking/CAS/revision, envelopes and exit mapping. Real production-adapter tests check isolated-store hashes, concurrent fields, no-op and unavailable refusal. No second domain, writer, transport or renderer is planned.

source_citations.excerpt:
### AC-008

**Criterion:** The settings CLI (008) reads and sets "Return to the dictation's application" with the same validation as the UI, including the unsupported-platform refusal. With `--json`, stdout contains only the JSON envelope.
**Priority:** P2 | **Story:** Story 5

plan_citations.excerpt: Add `return_to_dictation_app: bool` descriptor to 008's existing output domain and PublicSettings projection, rather than registering a second output domain.

UI command uses the same SettingsMutation and pure validation/capability guard; read_snapshot/commit_mutation use 008's same latest-state validation, expected revision, lock, durable persist and LiveSettingsEffects.
Return exactly 008 envelopes `{ok:true,revision:N,data:{...}}` or `{ok:false,error:{code,message,details:{...}}}` and existing exit mapping 0/1/2/3/4/5.
New `src-tauri/tests/destination_cli.rs` invokes real production CLI domain and UI command adapter with isolated stores and OS capability ports.

conclusions.rationale: Steps 1/2/4/7 cover capture at real successful start, own-process exclusion, immutable session state through recording/processing/AI and guarded explicit badge changes. Platform identity and process-start checks prevent display-name/PID redirection; session destination is volatile. Required native and state tests cover both normal and queued starts.

**Requirement:** Capture the destination application at dictation start, excluding Handy, and keep it stable for the whole dictation unless changed from the badge.
**AC References:** AC-001, AC-004

plan_citations.excerpt: Capture and selection stay unchanged through recording, processing and AI except explicit badge choices.
capture before overlay display and preserve through processing/AI.

conclusions.rationale: Activation orchestration is async and bounded independently of preserved method delays, with a single activation request and target/cancel recheck at first input dispatch. **AC References:** AC-002, AC-006

plan_citations.excerpt: New `destination/insertion.rs` orchestrates freeze/resolve/one-shot activation/async deadline.
Retain configured method behavior (direct, ctrl_v, shift_insert, ctrl_shift_v, external_script), delays, trailing-space, existing clipboard handling and legacy auto-submit semantics.

Dedicated nonactivating panels or approved resizing are selected by the native spike, not a normal focus-stealing menu. Frontend assertions, accessible labels and native focus measurements cover current-dictation-only choices under the deferred design gate.

source_citations.excerpt:
### FR-003

**Requirement:** Show a destination badge with icon, name and accessible label next to the indicator, and a non-activating menu to change the destination for the current dictation.
**AC References:** AC-003, AC-004

plan_citations.excerpt: Add a separate cross hit target and translated "Remove destination" label, consume its click without opening the menu, and reuse FrontmostAtEnd command/version guards; no persistent setting mutation.

Spike macOS NSPanel badge resizing and a separate nonactivating `destination_menu` webview panel (can_become_key_window=false); Windows no-activate HWND/WebView2 surface using WS_EX_NOACTIVATE and WM_MOUSEACTIVATE handling.

conclusions.rationale: Unavailable destination means zero new dispatch, no relaunch/retry/other-app fallback, retention of final text and truthful conditional history. Reasons and optional recovery handoff have guarded timing/acknowledgement, reference expiry and absent/duplicate/stale-consumer tests. Irreversible partial method input and volatile crash/supersession limits are stated without pretending a durable or atomic guarantee.

source_citations.excerpt:
### FR-004

**Requirement:** Never insert into another application when the destination is unavailable; preserve the transcript, report the reason and hand it to the recovery features.
**AC References:** AC-005

plan_citations.excerpt: **Action:** Modify actions.rs and destination/outcome.rs to retain final text and publish one truthful metadata outcome; record actual conditional history status.

Preserve the final text in the native recovery slot on destination failure even when history fails; keep latest unresolved outcome until superseded by a later final result, explicit consumer release or process exit.

conclusions.rationale: Destination attempted status is separate from exact method evidence, with no generic verified flag or plaintext event. The current AC-006 exception is respected through provenance of 007 inserted, verified, not destination certification. All eight results and terminal waiting are covered, clipboard restoration remains outside 006, and configuration domains retain destination/method/clipboard separation.

source_citations.excerpt:
### FR-005

**Requirement:** Report insertion outcomes as attempted, not verified, and keep destination, insertion method and clipboard handling separate.
**AC References:** AC-006

plan_citations.excerpt: No `verified` success flag.

007 is the smart-paste method result producer, not a recovery-window consumer: the InsertionPort awaits its direct read-back or clipboard read/no-read completion without blocking the UI and never turns transaction enqueue into a terminal success.
006 only adds return_to_dictation_app and neither implements 007's migration nor invents clipboard recovery settings.

conclusions.rationale: Capability, availability reason and the single persisted boolean reach both native UI and existing settings CLI through 008 names and domain layout. **AC References:** AC-007, AC-008
